stem: A newborn is assigned Apgar scores at 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth. Which set lists the five components used to calculate the Apgar score?

options.A: Heart rate, respiratory effort, blood pressure, temperature, and birth weight
options.B: Heart rate, respiratory effort, gestational age, birth weight, and head circumference
options.C: Heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood glucose, temperature, and muscle tone
options.D: Heart rate, respiratory effort, muscle tone, reflex irritability, and color

rationale: The joint ACOG/AAP statement defines the five Apgar components as color, heart rate, reflexes or reflex irritability, muscle tone, and respiration or respiratory effort. Blood pressure, temperature, birth weight, gestational age, head circumference, oxygen saturation, and blood glucose may be clinically relevant newborn data but are not components of the Apgar score.
educational_objective: Recall the five Apgar components: heart rate, respiratory effort, muscle tone, reflex irritability, and color.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP)
source_document_title: The Apgar Score — Committee Opinion No. 644
source_locator: Introduction, paragraph defining the five components and reporting at 1 and 5 minutes.
source_claim_supported: The reaffirmed joint ACOG/AAP statement lists color, heart rate, reflexes, muscle tone, and respiration as the five Apgar components and states that scores are reported at 1 and 5 minutes after birth.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation → acute physiological transition and newborn assessment content relevant to adaptation after birth.
